summary: A list of actions or options that opens from a button: row overflow actions, view options, sort order. Supports icons, shortcuts, groups, checkable items and submenus.
whenToUse: More than two or three actions on one item: show the main one as a button and the rest in a Menu.
View options: checkable items for columns, a radio group for sort order.
A submenu for one level of grouping (Move to group, then the groups).

Leading icons when they help scanning (Rename, Duplicate, Delete): pass icon, a Lucide icon or an element like a brand mark. Put icons on every item of the menu or on none; labels stay aligned either way.
whenNotToUse: Choosing a value for a form field: use Select or Combobox, which work with Field and forms.
Navigation between pages: use links in the sidebar or tabs.
Two actions: show both as buttons.

dos.title: Destructive items last, after a separator
dos.text: Distance from routine actions prevents slips. The danger tone backs up the verb.

dos.title: Icons on all items or on none
dos.text: Labels stay aligned either way, but a mix reads as noise.

donts.title: Submenus inside submenus
donts.text: Two levels deep loses keyboard and pointer users alike. Flatten with groups.

accessibility: Base UI Menu: the trigger has aria-haspopup and aria-expanded; the popup is role menu with menuitem, menuitemcheckbox and menuitemradio children.
ArrowDown or Enter opens it and focuses the first item; arrows move, Home and End jump, typing a letter jumps to a matching item.
Enter and Space activate; checkable items toggle aria-checked and keep the menu open.
ArrowRight opens a submenu, ArrowLeft and Escape close it; Escape on the root returns focus to the trigger.
Shortcut hints are visual only (aria-hidden); bind the shortcut yourself and document it elsewhere.
Disabled items stay in the list so users learn the action exists, but cannot be activated.
contentGuidelines: Items are verbs in sentence case: "Rename", "Duplicate", "Delete token".
Group labels are short nouns: "Columns", "Sort by".
No ellipsis on items, even when they open a dialog: the dialog title says what happens next.
